notes: Requested qal gloss was "borrow" alone, matching Deut.15.6 ("you shall not borrow") well, but the other qal citation (Deut.24.10, לַעֲבֹט עֲבֹטוֹ, "to take his pledge") describes the opposite direction -- a creditor exacting collateral, not a debtor borrowing. BDB's own (single) qal sense is actually "to take possession of a thing pledged", matching Deut.24.10 rather than the conventional "borrow" reading of Deut.15.6. Broadened the qal gloss to "borrow; take a pledge" to cover both attested citations honestly rather than force one citation under a gloss it doesn't support.

Requested piel sense was not included: the sole piel form (Joel.2.7, יְעַבְּטוּן) is textually obscure -- BDB calls it "hardly makes sense" and offers only a tentative guess ("lend on pledge = interchange?"). Given no confident gloss can be drawn from the citation, piel was left out of the paradigm; flagging for review rather than silently including or dropping it.
